contract: One paid order leads to exactly one fulfillment, even when the webhook is delivered more than once, concurrently, or under a different event ID; a failed fulfillment is never marked complete.

attempts.diagnosis: The handler only deduplicated on event.id, and only recorded the event after `await fulfillOrder` finished. Overlapping deliveries of the same event all passed the check before any of them recorded it. Events with different IDs for the same order never matched the cache at all. Both cases led to repeated fulfillment of one order.
attempts.changeSummary: Idempotency is now keyed on the order ID. A module-level Set holds orders whose fulfillment succeeded. A Map holds one in-flight fulfillment promise per order, and it is set synchronously before any await. Later deliveries for an order that is completed or in flight do not call fulfillOrder. In-flight waiters await the shared promise and return 'duplicate' once it succeeds. If it fails, they reject with the same error, so there is no fake acknowledgement. The order is added to the completed Set only after fulfillOrder succeeds, and the in-flight entry is always cleared afterwards, so a later retry fulfills exactly once.
